open_points.subject: A11 rule 3 (unknown outcome resolved as not_applied)
open_points.text: "the kernel writes one further NodeExecution with the next attempt number" ... "not_applied: no further NodeExecution"
open_points.question: When the owner resolves an unknown outcome as not_applied, is a new NodeExecution written for the resolution step or not?
options: Always write a resolution NodeExecution (including not_applied)
Write a resolution NodeExecution only for applied outcomes
Never write a resolution NodeExecution; only update EffectAttempt and waiting state
open_points.default_guess: Write no additional NodeExecution for not_applied.

open_points.subject: A11 attempt numbering across resolution and resend
open_points.text: A11 rule 3 says resolution writes "the next attempt number", but required test 3 says after resolving not_applied "the resend is attempt 2".
open_points.question: If not_applied resolution consumes an attempt number, what number should the subsequent resend use?
options: Resolution is attempt 2, resend is attempt 3
Resolution does not consume an attempt number, resend is attempt 2
open_points.default_guess: Resolution(not_applied) does not consume a new attempt number; resend is attempt 2.

open_points.subject: A11 rule 1 (what attempt_number counts)
open_points.text: "attempt_number counts from 1 every record the kernel writes about that element in order"
open_points.question: Which records are included in this count (NodeExecution only, EffectAttempt only, both, or additional run/wait records), and how can one send have both EffectAttempt and NodeExecution with the same number?
options: Count send-attempts, and assign the same number to EffectAttempt+NodeExecution of that send
Count every trace/store record and give each a unique number
Count only NodeExecution records
open_points.default_guess: Count logical attempts; EffectAttempt and its matching NodeExecution share one number.

open_points.subject: A16 request processing order
open_points.text: A16 rule 1 authenticates token on every request; A16 rule 4 says "Every request is validated against its schema before anything else happens".
open_points.question: Which check runs first: token authentication or request-schema/size validation?
options: Authenticate token first, then validate schema
Validate schema/size first, then authenticate
Perform both but guarantee indistinguishable refusals for unauthenticated callers
open_points.default_guess: Authenticate first, then schema-validate authorized request.

open_points.subject: A14 startup recovery for running non-read operation elements without a concluded record
open_points.text: "a function element without a concluded record is executed again ...; a `read` element without one is sent again."
open_points.question: At startup recovery, what is done for a non-read operation element in a running run if it has no concluded NodeExecution (and no durable in_flight record)?
options: Treat like read and send again
Move it to outcome_unknown and wait for owner resolution
Fail the run as internal inconsistency
Refuse startup until manual repair
open_points.default_guess: Mark as outcome_unknown and wait for owner resolution.

open_points.subject: A09 pre-send local refusal mapping
open_points.text: "An absolute path, a change of host, userinfo or a fragment is refused before anything is sent."
open_points.question: When this refusal happens during run execution, which NodeExecution status and waiting behavior are recorded (operation_failed, contract_violation, service_unreachable, immediate run failure, etc.)?
options: Record operation_failed (local policy refusal) and continue failure propagation
Record contract_violation
Record service_unreachable and allow resume
Treat as request-level refusal without NodeExecution
open_points.default_guess: Record operation_failed with a specific local-refusal detail.

open_points.subject: A07 rule 5 execution class used for failure_detail redaction
open_points.text: "returned to an agent only as its length and the execution's class."
open_points.question: How is "execution's class" computed and stored for NodeExecution, since M23 does not define a class field?
options: Derive as max disclosure class of execution inputs
Derive as max of inputs and outputs
Add an explicit class field to NodeExecution
Compute on read each time from referenced values
open_points.default_guess: Use max input disclosure class, computed on read if not stored.
